text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police are hunting for seven awaiting-trial prisoners who on Thursday escaped from custody at a police station in Machinga district in southern Malawi.
- A vigilante group policing a Blantyre township has sent shock waves of terror as its members face accusations of gang-raping women found walking in the streets late at night.

- A Chinese company Xinhua at the on-going international trade exhibition in Blantyre has attracted a large crowd at its pavilion with an HIV/AIDS drug, "Conthy Capsule", a novel natural Chinese medicine which the company claims treats and prevents HIV infection development.

- Public Prosecutor Kamudoni Nyasulu said on Sunday that a Blantyre-based businessman implicated in a 38 million kwacha bank fraud would only be arrested if police were satisfied that they had a good case against him.

- A prominent Blantyre businessman mentioned in a 38 million kwacha bank fraud won full backing of police chief Patrick Chikapa who said on Sunday that nobody had complained to the police about his alleged criminal beaviour.
- Seven suspects on various criminal charges on Wednesday escaped from a police cell in Machinga, southern Malawi, and were reported to be still at large by the weekend.
